short: Goods a customer sends back after being billed.
seoTitle: Sales Return — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: A sales return is stock a customer returns after billing, whether damaged, wrong or simply unwanted. Goods a customer sends back after being billed.
definition: A sales return is stock a customer returns after billing, whether damaged, wrong or simply unwanted. It reduces net sales, brings the goods back into stock, and reverses the tax charged through a credit note.
bodyHtml:
Why Sales Return matters

Returns handled informally leave three things wrong at once: overstated sales, understated stock and GST paid on revenue you did not keep.

Sales Return formula

Return rate % = Value of returns ÷ Gross sales × 100

Track it by product to find quality or description problems.

How Sales Return works in practice

Issue a credit note against the original invoice, take the goods back into stock at cost, and separate resaleable returns from write-offs so stock value stays honest.

faq.question: Do I need a credit note for a return?
faq.answer: Yes, if a tax invoice was issued. That is what reverses the GST on the original sale.

faq.question: Should returned goods go back at full value?
faq.answer: Only if genuinely resaleable. Damaged returns should be written down or written off.
